transcript:
Header:
2026-11-18 09:32 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Sofia Alvarez, Noah Kim, Priya Shah, Ethan Lopez (BrightBridge)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on planning the rollout/cutover for BrightBridge pilot to production. Covered canary design, A/B tradeoffs, metrics to watch, runbook ownership, and security signoffs.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we can kick off. Today is mainly rollout planning - canary, cutover, monitoring, runbooks. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia here, good morning.
[00:08] Noah Kim: Noah on the platform side.
[00:09] Priya Shah: Priya from security.
[00:11] Ethan Lopez: Ethan, data science.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: Ravi, SE from Redwood.
[00:13] Lena Ortiz: Lena, CSM.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Great. I'll hand off to Ravi for a quick perf recap then we'll move into canary strategy.

[02:02] Ravi Patel: Cool, thanks Maya. So since last week we re-ran the load tests with the quantized model bundle on g4dn-equivalent nodes - uh, sorry, some labeling in the spreadsheet says g4x but it's actually the g5-type instance we used. Anyway, 95th percentile latency for the 1k-token prompts is around 220ms, 99th is ~470ms under steady-state. The KV cache hit rate improved to ~58% after the prefix caching tweak - you may see the labels say "KV cash" in the sheet, that's a transcription artifact.
[03:00] Sofia Alvarez: When you say steady-state, what input mix are we using? Our production will have a lot more short prompts - templated queries from the triage UI.
[03:10] Ravi Patel: Good point. The test blend was 60% short (under 50 tokens), 30% medium (50-300), 10% long. If your live mix is heavier on shorts we'll see better median latencies, but the 99th might be more variable unless we control batch sizing.
[03:35] Noah Kim: On the platform side we need the exact autoscaler thresholds - we ran into flapping in the staging cluster last week when traffic spiked and the pod startup time was longer than expected.
[03:46] Maya Chen: Right, we saw that. Ravi, can you remind the team of the recommended autoscale policy?
[03:50] Ravi Patel: Yeah, recommend target CPU at 65%, scale window 90s, and a warm pool of one extra instance per shard to avoid cold start. For Dedicated customers we also suggest a burst pool - that reduces tail latency on spikes.
[04:10] Priya Shah: On security, two things: we need confirmation on KMS integration for envelope encryption - will Redwood support customer-managed KMS in the VPC/private install? Also SOC2 scope: do you provide audit logs for per-request metadata?
[04:28] Maya Chen: Short answer: yes to CMK support in Private; for hosted we'll provide a HSM-backed option for enterprise. Audit logs are available and include model version, route, timestamps; Ravi can confirm fields.
[04:40] Ravi Patel: Yep, the logs include request id, model id, user id (if passed), latency, and route. There was an earlier bug where model name sometimes showed as "RW-model-0" in logs, but that is fixed in the latest build.
[05:02] Sofia Alvarez: Great. For rollout itself, we want a canary that runs on 5% of traffic for 48 hours, then 25% for 24 hours if no regressions, then full cutover. We also want an A/B comparison on quality for a labeled subset. Thoughts?
[05:20] Ravi Patel: That sounds reasonable. A/B gives you direct quality comparison but increases risk since two models are live. Canary is safer operationally. For your use-case I'd recommend canary + a shadow A/B on labeled traffic - run the canary model for real responses for 5% while also scoring the primary model on the labeled subset so you get ROC/precision metrics.
[05:45] Ethan Lopez: How do we handle rollback criteria? It's important for product to have clear thresholds - e.g., 5% increase in error rate or a 20% regression in our F1 on the labeled set.
[05:56] Maya Chen: We'll propose concrete thresholds in the runbook. Typical ones: 5xx error rate > 0.5% above baseline, latency 99p > 30% over baseline, and labeled-quality drop > X% (you define X).
[06:12] Noah Kim: Also add cost per 1k-token change - procurement asks if the new model doubles inference spend.
[06:18] Ravi Patel: We'll include cost delta in the dashboard; our perf spreadsheet includes tokens/sec and estimated cost per 1k tokens for the selected instance types.
[06:30] Priya Shah: About monitoring - what out-of-the-box dashboards will Redwood provide versus what we need to add in our Grafana?
[06:38] Lena Ortiz: We have default dashboards for latency percentiles, errors, throughput, KV cache hit rate, and model version traffic split. Those can be exported to your Grafana via our telemetry exporter.
[06:48] Ravi Patel: We'll also include a canary health endpoint and synthetic check scripts - e.g., run synthetic inference every minute and compare to expected top-K tokens.
[07:00] Sofia Alvarez: Cool. Can we get a sample runbook structure?
[07:05] Maya Chen: That's an action item - I'll share a draft. It will include pre-checks, canary steps, rollback, post-cutover validation, and stakeholders.
[07:12] Ravi Patel: I'll attach the perf spreadsheet with the corrected labels; look for the tab named "final_perf_v2".
[10:22] Noah Kim: Quick question about routing and feature flags - when we shift traffic we want to do it at the edge so sessions pin correctly. Does Redwood support sticky routing for users?
[10:34] Ravi Patel: We have per-route session affinity when you pass a session key; otherwise routing is random. For predictable user-level canaries pass user_id as session key and the router will honor affinity.
[13:00] Priya Shah: On compliance again - Priya: will you provide documentation for encryption at rest and in transit for the Dedicated offering? We need details for our security review board.
[13:10] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the security pack including KMS options, TLS cipher suite details, and data residency notes. Lena, please add to the next steps.
[18:40] Ethan Lopez: For the labeled A/B tests, we need a way to collect the model outputs and have them side-by-side in our evaluation UI. Any integrations?
[18:50] Ravi Patel: You can stream responses to your evaluation endpoint in parallel via our webhook; we also support a shadow logging mode that adds both outputs to logs for later scoring. There might be a small token cost in shadow mode.
[23:55] Sofia Alvarez: Let's talk canary windows and rollback time. Our ops team wants to keep canaries during low-traffic windows to reduce blast radius. We were thinking of running the 5% canary 02:00-06:00 PT and then observe for two business cycles before increasing.
[24:12] Maya Chen: That works; the runbook will recommend scheduling during low traffic and running synthetics. Also include a manual hold point at each traffic increase.
[29:30] Ravi Patel: A note on KV cache priming - for templated prompts you can pre-warm KV caches by replaying a small sample of typical prefixes during the warm window; that reduces tail latency significantly. We can give you a script.
[29:47] Noah Kim: We'll want that script. Also we need the warm pool sizing recommendations for our shard count - current staging has 6 shards.
[29:56] Ravi Patel: For six shards, I'd suggest one warm extra instance per shard and two global burst instances.
[33:00] Priya Shah: Deliverables for security review: SAML SSO diagram, audit log schema, KMS options, and any SOC2 in-scope controls. We need those by next week to hit our internal gate.
[33:12] Maya Chen: Understood - Priya, we'll send the pack by Friday.
[36:40] Sofia Alvarez: On stakeholder coordination: who from Redwood will be on the cutover call? We want an SE and an AE at minimum.
[36:48] Maya Chen: I'll be on the cutover and Ravi will own the technical run. Lena will coordinate the post-cutover validation.
[40:05] Ethan Lopez: One more: can we run a tabletop dry-run next Tuesday? We'll simulate a rollback and check our alerting.
[40:15] Maya Chen: Yes, that's a good call. Action item: Sofia to confirm participants and time.
[43:00] Maya Chen: OK let's recap next steps - I'll share runbook + canary template, Ravi sends perf sheet, Priya will list security artifacts, Sofia confirms dry-run. Any final questions?
[43:15] Priya Shah: None from me.
[43:18] Noah Kim: All good.
[43:20] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks everyone.
[43:28] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the documents.

[End of call]
